cards.front: Recall a key point about US Independent Film
cards.back: US independent film is produced outside the major Hollywood studio system, typically with lower budgets, creative freedom and alternative approaches to narrative, representation and style.

cards.front: Recall a key point about US Independent Film
cards.back: Independent filmmaking often prioritises personal vision, artistic experimentation and social relevance over commercial considerations and mass audience appeal.

cards.front: Recall a key point about US Independent Film
cards.back: Key indie aesthetics include naturalistic performance, location shooting, handheld cinematography, non-linear narratives and ambiguous endings that challenge mainstream conventions.

cards.front: Recall a key point about US Independent Film
cards.back: The Sundance Film Festival, founded by Robert Redford in 1978, became the premier showcase for American independent film and a launchpad for indie careers and distribution.

cards.front: Recall a key point about US Independent Film
cards.back: Independent films frequently explore subjects avoided by mainstream Hollywood — marginalised communities, social problems, complex identities — offering perspectives that challenge dominant ideologies.

cards.front: Recall a key point about US Independent Film
cards.back: Low budgets can be a creative strength, forcing innovative solutions: location shooting instead of studio sets, unknown actors instead of stars, and practical effects instead of CGI spectacle.

cards.front: Recall a key point about US Independent Film
cards.back: The boundary between indie and mainstream has blurred as major studios create indie divisions — Fox Searchlight, Focus Features — that produce arthouse-style films within corporate structures.

cards.front: Recall a key point about US Independent Film
cards.back: Independent distribution relies on film festivals, arthouse cinemas, limited releases and word-of-mouth marketing rather than the saturation campaigns used for blockbusters.

cards.front: Recall a key point about US Independent Film
cards.back: US independent film has produced some of the most critically acclaimed and culturally significant American films, from Easy Rider to Moonlight, proving that commercial constraints are not necessary for artistic impact.

cards.front: Recall a key point about US Independent Film
cards.back: Comparing indie and mainstream films reveals how budget, institutional context and audience expectations shape every aspect of filmmaking from narrative structure to visual style.

cards.front: Recall a key point about US Independent Film
cards.back: The indie aesthetic has itself become a marketable brand, with some mainstream films adopting surface indie characteristics while retaining conventional Hollywood narrative and ideological frameworks.

cards.front: Recall a key point about US Independent Film
cards.back: Digital technology has democratised independent filmmaking by reducing production costs, enabling wider distribution through streaming platforms and allowing diverse voices to reach audiences previously excluded.
